==English==
{{wikipedia}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|cvt||censored spelling}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:cutten|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|cutten}}, of {{der|en|gmq}} origin, from {{der|en|non|*kytja}}, {{m|non|*kutta}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*kutjaną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*kuttaną|t=to cut}}, of uncertain origin, perhaps related to {{der|en|gem-pro|*kwetwą|t=meat, flesh}} (compare {{cog|non|kvett|t=meat}}). Sometimes instead compared to {{cog|fr|couteau}}, itself from {{cog|la|culter|t=knife}}.<ref>{{R:Online_Etymology_Dictionary}}</ref>

Compare {{cog|sco|kut}}, {{m|sco|kit|t=to cut}}); also akin to Middle {{cog|sv|kotta|t=to cut or carve with a knife}} (compare dialectal {{cog|sv|kåta}}, {{m|sv|kuta|t=to cut or chip with a knife}}, {{cog|sv|kuta}}, {{m|sv|kytti|t=a knife}}), {{cog|nb|kutte|t=to cut}}, {{cog|nn|kutte|t=to cut}}, {{cog|is|kuta|t=to cut with a knife}}, {{cog|non|kuti|t=small knife}}, {{cog|no|kyttel}}, {{m|no|kytel}}, {{m|no|kjutul|t=pointed slip of wood used to strip bark}}. {{displaced|enm|snithen}} (from {{m|ang|snīþan}}), still attested in dialectal {{m|en|snithe}} and {{m|en|snead}}. See {{m|en|snide}}.

The adjective sense of "drunk" (now rare and now usually used in the originally humorous derivative form of {{m|en|half-cut}}) dates from the 17th century, from {{m|en||cut in the leg}} or {{m|en||to have cut your leg}}, a {{lg|euphemism}} for being very drunk.

===Verb===
{{en-verb|~s|~ting|~,~ted<l:nonstandard,archaic>|+,~ten<l:archaic>}}

# {{lb|en|mostly|transitive}} To [[incise]], to cut into the surface of something.
## To [[perform]] an [[incision]] on, for example with a [[knife]].
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|act=IV|scene=i|passage=You must '''cut''' this flesh from off his breast.}}
##* {{quote-av|en|year=1969|year_published=1969|writer=w:Jerome Bixby|title=w:Star Trek: The Original Series|episode=w:Day of the Dove|season=[[w:Star Trek: The Original Series season 3|3]]|number=7|location=Culver City, California|publisher={{w|Desilu Studios}}; distributed by {{w|Paramount Television}}
|passage=Mara: We are forty against four hundred. // Klingon: Four thousand throats may be '''cut''' in one night by a running man.}}
## To [[divide]] with a [[knife]], [[scissors]], or another [[sharp]] [[instrument]].
##: {{uxi|en|Would you please '''cut''' the cake?}}
##* {{RQ:Homer Pope et al Odyssey|book=III|passage=Before the whistling winds the vessels fly, / With rapid swiftness '''cut''' the liquid way.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|date=8 May 2012|title=Ottolenghi: The Cookbook|author=w:Yotam Ottolenghi; Sami Tamimi|publisher=w:Random House|isbn=9781446407097|url=https://books.google.co.nz/books?id=WFzJR9ZZ7aEC|page=79
|passage=First, marinate the tofu. In a bowl, whisk the kecap manis, chilli sauce, and sesame oil together. '''Cut''' the tofu into strips about 1cm thick, mix gently (so it doesn't break) with the marinade and leave in the fridge for half an hour.}}
## To [[form]] or [[shape]] by cutting.
##: {{uxi|en|I have three diamonds to '''cut''' today.}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|act=I|scene=i|passage=Why should a man, whose blood is warm within, / Sit like his grandsire '''cut''' in alabaster}}
##* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=8|passage=loopholes '''cut''' through thickest shade|year=1873}}
## {{lb|en|slang}} To [[wound]] with a knife.
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1990|author=w:Stephen Dobyns|title=The house on Alexandrine
|passage=We don't want your money no more. We just going to '''cut''' you.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To engage in [[self-harm]] by making cuts in one's own skin.
##: {{uxi|en|The patient said she had been '''cutting''' since the age of thirteen.}}
##* {{quote-song|en|date=2023-07-18|author={{w|Noelle Stockwood}} [{{w|Femtanyl}}]|title=PUSH UR T3MPRR|album=CHASER
|passage=I was inspired not to '''cu-cu-cu-cut''' / When you told me that you wanna see}}
## {{lb|en|ambitransitive}} To deliver a [[stroke]] with a [[whip]] or like instrument to.
##* {{RQ:Ferguson Zollenstein|IV
|passage=“My Continental prominence is improving,” I commented dryly. ¶ Von Lindowe '''cut''' at a furze bush with his silver-mounted rattan. ¶ “Quite so,” he said as dryly, his hand at his mustache. “I may say if your intentions were known your life would not be worth a curse.”}}
## To wound or hurt deeply the sensibilities of; to pierce.
##: {{ux|en|Sarcasm '''cuts''' to the quick.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1829|author=Elijah Hoole|title=Personal Narrative of a Mission to the South of India, from 1820 to 1828
|passage=she feared she should laugh to hear an European preach in Tamul , but on the contrary , was '''cut''' to the heart by what she heard}}
## To [[castrate]] or [[geld]].
##: {{ux|en|to '''cut''' a horse}}
## To [[interfere]], as a horse; to strike one foot against the opposite foot or ankle in using the legs.
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To admit of incision or severance; to yield to a cutting instrument.
#* {{RQ:Holmes Autocrat|chapter=The Deacon's Masterpiece|passage=The panels of white-wood that '''cuts''' like cheese, / But lasts like iron for things like these;}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|social}} ''To [[separate]], [[remove]], [[reject]] or [[reduce]].''
## To [[separate]] or [[omit]], in a situation where one was [[previous]]ly [[associated]].
##: {{ux|en|Travis was '''cut''' from the team.}}
## To [[abridge]] or [[shorten]] a work; to remove a portion of a [[recording]] during [[editing]].
## To [[reduce]], especially intentionally.
##: {{ux|en|They're going to '''cut''' salaries by fifteen percent.}}
## To absent oneself from (a class, an appointment, etc.).
##: {{ux|en|I '''cut''' fifth period to hang out with Angela.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1833|author={{w|Thomas Hamilton (writer)|Thomas Hamilton}}|title=Men and Manners in America|passage=An English tradesman is always solicitous to '''cut''' the shop whenever he can do so with impunity.}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive|slang}} To [[leave#Verb|leave]] abruptly.
##: {{syn|en|dip<q:slang>}}
##: {{ux|en|I gotta '''cut''' but I'll see you tomorrow, okay?}}
##* {{RQ:Twitter|en|date=3 September 2023|handle=tamashbean|id=1698323886751047914|passage=my friends and i had gone for lunch but i had to '''cut''' early and couldn't get dessert (which if you know me it's my top priority) so they got it packed and dropped off at my place without a word "open the lift and take it" ?????????? how is this real i will literally cry}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|social}} To [[ignore]] as a social [[rebuff]] or [[snub]].
#: {{syn|en|spear}}
#: {{ux|en|After the incident at the dinner party, people started to '''cut''' him on the street.}}
#* {{Q|en|Samuel Barber|The Way of All Flesh|chapter 73|year=1903|quote=At first it had been very painful to him to meet any of his old friends, [...] but this soon passed; either they '''cut''' him, or he '''cut''' them; it was not nice being '''cut''' for the first time or two, but after that, it became rather pleasant than not [...] The ordeal is a painful one, but if a man's moral and intellectual constitution are naturally sound, there is nothing which will give him so much strength of character as having been well '''cut'''.}}
#* {{Q|en|Gore Vidal|Burr|year=1973|quote=The ordinary people greet him ''(Aaron Burr)'' warmly while the respectable folk tend '''to cut''' him dead.}}
#* {{Q|en|Kane, Kathryn|The Regency Redingote Blog|The Cut: The Ultimate & Final Social Weapon|year=27 September 2013|quote=The Monthly Magazine, Or, British Register for 1798 included an explanation by a reader of how the cut was carried out in his college days in a lengthy letter to the editor, signed by the pseudonym "Ansonius." In his rambling letter, Ansonius noted that when he was at college, ''" … if a man passed an old acquaintance wittingly, without recognizing him, he was said— ‘'''To cut''' him.’"'' Ansonius then went on to explain the performance of the cut and noted that for a time the term "to spear" was used instead of to cut. However, that term did not remain long in use, and this act was generally known as "the cut" ever after.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|cinema}} To make an abrupt transition from one [[scene]] or image to another.
#: {{ux|en|The camera then '''cut''' to the woman on the front row who was clearly overcome and crying tears of joy.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|film}} To [[edit]] a film by selecting [[takes]] from original [[footage]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|computing}} To [[remove]] (text, a picture, etc.) and place in [[memory]] in order to [[paste]] at a later time.
#: {{ux|en|Select the text, '''cut''' it, and then paste it in the other application.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[enter]] a [[queue]] in the wrong place.
#: {{ux|en|One student kept trying to '''cut''' in front of the line.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[intersect]] or [[cross]] in such a way as to [[divide]] in [[half]] or nearly so.
#: {{ux|en|This road '''cuts''' right through downtown.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=January 18, 2011|author=Daniel Taylor| title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/football/2011/jan/18/manchester-city-leicester-city-fa-cup Manchester City 4 Leicester City 2]| passage=Neither Joleon Lescott nor Vieira appeared to make any contact with Dyer as he '''cut''' between them.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|cricket}} To make the ball spin sideways by running one's [[finger]]s down the side of the ball while bowling it. {{rfex|en}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|cricket}} To [[deflect]] (a bowled ball) to the [[off]], with a chopping movement of the [[bat]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To change [[direction]] suddenly.
#: {{ux|en|The football player '''cut''' to his left to evade a tackle.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To [[divide]] a [[pack]] of [[playing card]]s into two parts, often followed by placing the two parts back together in the opposite order.
#: {{ux|en|If you '''cut''' then I'll deal.}}
# {{sid|en|to conclude}} {{lb|en|transitive|slang}} To [[make]], [[negotiate]]; to [[finalise]], [[conclude]]; to [[issue]].
#: {{ux|en|I'll '''cut''' a check for you.}}
#: {{ux|en|I didn't deserve it, but he '''cut''' me a deal.}}
#: {{coi|en|to '''cut''' a deal, to '''cut''' deals}}
#: {{coi|en|to '''cut''' a fantastic deal, to '''cut''' a raw deal}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|slang}} To [[dilute]] or [[adulterate]] something, especially a recreational drug.
#: {{ux|en|The best malt whiskies are improved if they are '''cut''' with a dash of water.}}
#: {{ux|en|The bartender '''cuts''' his beer to save money and now it's all watery.}}
#: {{ux|en|Drug dealers sometimes '''cut''' cocaine with lidocaine.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To exhibit (a figure having some trait).
#: {{ux|en|The Bender family '''cut''' a very distinct profile.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[stop]], [[disengage]]{{,}} or [[cease]].
#: {{syn|en|cut out}}
#: {{ux|en|The schoolchildren were told to '''cut''' the noise.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Cut''' the engines when the plane comes to a halt!}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[renounce]] or [[give up]]. <!--Chambers 1908-->
#: {{syn|en|cut out}}
# {{lb|en|sports}} To drive (a [[ball]]) to one side, as by (in billiards or croquet) hitting it [[fine]] with another ball, or (in tennis) striking it with the racket inclined.
# {{sid|en|losemass}} {{lb|en|bodybuilding}} To [[lose]] [[body mass]], aiming to keep [[muscle]] but lose [[body fat]].
#: {{cot|en|bulk|id1=gainmass}}
# To perform (an elaborate dancing movement etc.).
#: ''to [[cut a caper]]''
# {{lb|en|colloquial|intransitive}} To [[run]] or [[hurry]].
#* {{RQ:Kipling Diversity of Creatures|story=The Honours of War|page=114|passage=‘Look here, you're nearest his size. '''Cut''' up to your rooms and give Ipps your dinner things and a clean shirt for him.’}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1950|author=Frank Richards|title=Billy Bunter's Benefit
|passage=Now one of us had better '''cut''' down to Courtfield on a bike {{...}}}}
